classification.difficultyReason: Use perimeter to express one side in terms of the other, form an area equation and interpret its two roots as the side lengths.

content.prompt: A rectangular field is $405\text{ m}^2$ in area, and its perimeter is $200\text{ m}$. Find the length of its sides. Give your answers correct to two decimal places.

answer.short:
$50-\sqrt{2095}\text{ m}$ and $50+\sqrt{2095}\text{ m}$, approximately $4.23\text{ m}$ and $95.77\text{ m}$.

Use the perimeter to express the sides as $x$ and $100-x$, then solve the area equation.
answer.worked:
Let one side be $x$ metres and the other be $y$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}2x+2y&=200\\x+y&=100\\y&=100-x\end{align*}$$
Using the area,
$$\begin{align*}x(100-x)&=405\\x^2-100x+405&=0\\x^2-100x&=-405\\x^2-100x+2500&=2095\\(x-50)^2&=2095\\x&=50\pm\sqrt{2095}.\end{align*}$$
The two values exchange the roles of the sides. Both are positive.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Shorter side}&=50-\sqrt{2095}\text{ m}\approx4.23\text{ m}\\\text{Longer side}&=50+\sqrt{2095}\text{ m}\approx95.77\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
Check using the exact values: their sum is $100$, so the perimeter is $200\text{ m}$, and their product is $2500-2095=405$, giving the required area.
